sequence_description: I2 anti-replay: send a SAML assertion containing OneTimeUse and replay the exact same Assertion/@ID; second login should be rejected if OneTimeUse is enforced.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_i2_2_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_i2_2_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replay of a OneTimeUse SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID), violating anti-replay.

sequence_description: I2 anti-replay: replay the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID when the assertion omits <Conditions>. Even without OneTimeUse, a robust SP may still enforce replay protection via assertion ID cache; second acceptance indicates replay window/anti-replay missing.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_saml_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_saml_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted a replayed SAML assertion with the same Assertion/@ID (anti-replay not enforced).

sequence_description: I3 state swap / session splicing via SAML broker: perform two SAML logins with different upstream principals and swap the 'state' parameter between them. The broker should bind state to the correct in-flight session and reject mismatched state.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_saml_A_swapped_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_saml_A_swapped_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML login accepted with swapped state value, indicating state/session not coherently bound (state swap / session splicing).
